title: Canonicalizer + interruptible-output harness for JSON-mode fidelity and graceful carry-forward
creator: Ananya Rao
description: Build a deterministic test harness and runtime 'canonicalizer' to validate JSON-mode enforcement across partial/interruptible streams and interleaved tool/function calls. The harness will fuzz prompt prefixes and simulate mid-stream cancellations, token drops, and tool-call interleaving while asserting schema-level invariants and graceful degradation (well-formed partial object, sentinel metadata, or deterministic fallback). This ticket covers infra, test vectors, CI jobs, and a first-pass integration with the streaming decoder and runtime gate.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalizer component implemented: accepts token-level stream fragments and emits a canonical JSON AST or a documented fallback token stream representation
Fuzz corpus: 2000 synthetic prompts covering nested objects, optional fields, arrays, and tool-calling sequences; metadata for expected canonical forms
CI job: runs fast-smoke (200 vectors) on PRs and nightly full-run (2000 vectors) with pass/fail thresholds defined

Graceful degradation policy enforced: on partial stream interrupts the runtime emits either a well-formed partial JSON (with _incomplete:true) or a deterministic error object matching the schema contract
Telemetry events: schema_violation, canonicalize_latency_ms, fallback_reason are emitted for failing cases and surfaced on console QA dashboard
Integration: gating adapter toggles (canary) exist so feature can be enabled for runtime-1.24 canaries without affecting mainline
test_plan_steps: Implement canonicalizer library (JS/TS) with deterministic normalization rules (key ordering, whitespace removal, sentinel insertion)
Write streaming harness to replay token fragments into constrained decoder and canonicalizer in sequences (normal completion, mid-stream cancel, token drop, resumed stream)
Create interleaved-tool-call scenarios where tool-return payloads arrive out-of-order and verify canonicalizer/sanitizer handles embedded JSON tool outputs
Add mutation engine to perturb tokens (drop 1-3 tokens, introduce stray commas/brackets) and assert canonicalizer either repairs to contract or emits documented fallback
Hook telemetry: instrument canonicalizer with latency and failure reason tags; add simple dashboard in Console QA space
Author PR with tests + update release notes for runtime-1.24 canary toggle and provide runbook for investigating failing vectors
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed — prototyped canonicalizer normalization rules; chosen approach to produce canonical AST rather than naive string patching
2026-03-03: Fuzz corpus seeded with 500 vectors (nested arrays, optional fields). Early runs show ~12% repairable token-drop cases
2026-03-06: Decision to emit _incomplete:true sentinel on partial outputs accepted in design review with PM and Runtime eng
2026-03-09: Streaming harness integration finished for basic cases; failing interleaved tool-return scenarios identified (race in toolcall reassembly) — added locking heuristic
2026-03-12: End-to-end smoke tests (200 vectors) pass locally; PR opened (GH PR #redwood/infra/1489) — requesting runtime and SDK reviews
decisions: Canonicalizer will operate at the token-stream layer (pre-parse) to avoid repeated parse/serialize cycles and to preserve streaming latency characteristics
We will prefer a small deterministic repair set (insert missing closing brackets, normalize stray commas) rather than aggressive auto-correction to avoid altering user intent

For tool/function call interleaving, the harness will treat tool-return blocks as opaque until validated by canonicalizer; a 'reassembly window' of 250ms is used to await late tokens before emitting fallback
Feature gating: roll out behind runtime-1.24 canary flag to measure cost and false-positive rate before full flip
risks_mitigations: Risk: Repair heuristics might mask real semantic errors and lead to silent behavior changes — Mitigation: all repairs create telemetry events and a human-readable repair_summary field in the fallback object
Risk: Extra processing may increase p50 latency — Mitigation: canonicalizer implemented in hot-path-friendly JS with a native shim option planned for P2 if latency impact >5ms
Risk: Interleaved toolcalls create race conditions — Mitigation: reassembly window and watermarking applied; add deterministic tests for clock-skewed tool responses
Risk: CI run time growth — Mitigation: fast-smoke subset run on PRs, full corpus nightly with alerting and bucketing of flaky vectors
